summary: Satoshi Hayashima specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2013) and served there as a lecturer (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, and Luis Oscar Gómez. He held posts at Bukkyo University, Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, and Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Satoshi Kono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he served as an assistant professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).

Satya Swarup Misra works in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

Satya Vrat Shastri was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Punjabi University (~1949–1953) and Banaras Hindu University (~1953–1956), and held posts at the University of Delhi (~1961–1995) and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Hindu School, Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He held academic posts at the University of Dhaka, the University of Calcutta, and served as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

Buddhist studies scholar Sayadaw U Sģlānanda studied under U Paññāvanta and Mahasi Sayadaw. He held leadership posts at Mahāvijjodaya Chaung Monastery, Atithokdayone Pali University, the Theravada Buddhist Society of America, Dhammananda Vihara, and the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University.
Sayaka Sonoda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under doctoral supervisor Shinobu Yamaguchi and committee member Shogo Watanabe.

Scott A. Mitchell specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008) and became a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).
Scott Dalby works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and served as a lecturer at Amsterdam University College (attested 2014).

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his doctorate at the Australian National University in 2011, held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and lectured at the University of Manchester.

Sean D. Gaffney works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post at SOAS University of London and completed his PhD there under Tadeusz Skorupski, having also studied under Philip Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg.
See Mui Yian is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Cambridge (~1987–1991) and later held academic posts at the University of Delhi (~2008–2020) and Ashoka University (~2020).

Seigai Omura specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893) and served as a professor at Tokyo School of Fine Arts (~1902–1927).
Seiichi Mizuno was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and later served as a professor there (~1949–1968).
Seiichiro Ono was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1914–1917). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1952) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1956–1968).

Seiji Kimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986), where he also held a post (attested 1990), and later served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2003–2008) and became an associate professor there around 2014.
